headline: PALADIN ENERGY DISCOVERS 4.25% U₃O₈ ATLAS ZONE AT PLS — SECOND HIGH-GRADE FRONT 3.5km FROM TRIPLE R (ASX:PDN, TSX:PDN)
snippet: Paladin Energy confirmed June 25, 2026 the discovery of a new high-grade uranium body at Patterson Lake South in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin — the Atlas discovery — located 3.5km south of the Triple R deposit and 4.5km southwest of Saloon East, with 7 of 8 exploration drillholes intersecting significant uranium mineralisation. Discovery hole PLS26-708B returned 8.0m averaging 1.75% U₃O₈ including 3.0m at 4.25% U₃O₈ from 190.0m depth. Atlas remains open along strike and at depth, opening a second high-grade exploration front at one of the world's highest-grade undeveloped uranium projects — an asset already advancing toward production with the Triple R deposit at its core.

headline: OMAI GOLD DRILLS 7.26 g/t AU OVER 34.8m AT WENOT — PEA IN 4-6 WEEKS AS 5-RIG 50,000m GUYANA PROGRAM ACCELERATES (TSXV:OMG)
snippet: Omai Gold Mines Corp. (TSXV:OMG, OTCQB:OMGGF) released June 24 assays from six additional drill holes at the Omai Project in Guyana, with highlight hole 26ODD-185 returning 7.26 g/t gold over 34.8 metres across 15 discrete gold zones from 200 to 540m depth in the Wenot deposit. With 27,770m drilled across 58 holes year-to-date using five active rigs, 93–95% gold recovery confirmed in metallurgical tests, and a Preliminary Economic Assessment integrating the Wenot open pit and Gilt underground deposits targeted in 4–6 weeks, every new drill result is a potential NAV-driver ahead of an imminent resource-to-value conversion event.

headline: CHINA BLACKLISTS MP MATERIALS AND USA RARE EARTH — BREAKS BUSAN TRUCE, TARGETS FIRMS BACKED BY $2.15B IN U.S. GOVERNMENT FUNDING
snippet: China's Ministry of Commerce added MP Materials (NYSE:MP) and USA Rare Earth (USAR) to its export control blacklist on June 22, 2026, targeting the two largest recipients of U.S. government investment in domestic rare earth independence — $550M and $1.6B in federal backing respectively — and breaking the one-year critical minerals truce agreed at the October 2025 Busan summit. A June 24 Foundation for Defense of Democracies analysis argues the move is designed to specifically undermine the strategic intent of Western rare earth diversification and will chill third-country investment in alternative supply chains, since Chinese retaliation is now demonstrably directed at the most-funded U.S. mine-to-magnet beneficiaries.

headline: 5 DAYS TO COPPER TARIFF VERDICT: LUTNICK'S JUNE 30 DEADLINE COULD LOCK IN 15–30% REFINED IMPORT DUTIES FROM 2027
snippet: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick faces a June 30, 2026 statutory deadline to recommend whether to impose phased universal import duties on refined copper — 15% from January 1, 2027 and 30% from January 1, 2028 — the final unresolved copper trade policy decision that directly affects North American development project economics. With the U.S. importing approximately 57% of its refined copper and Goldman Sachs assigning high probability to a positive recommendation, a June 30 confirmation would increase the domestic copper price premium for North American producers and accelerate the investment case for the Canadian and BC copper development pipeline at a time when supply disruptions at Grasberg and Kamoa are already tightening the market.

headline: PwC MINE 2026: TOP 40 GLOBAL MINERS POST $909B REVENUES AND $120B PROFITS — BUYBACKS SURGE 252%, EBITDA AT 27%
snippet: PwC's annual Mine 2026 report, released June 25, found the world's top 40 mining companies generated revenues of US$909 billion in 2025 — up 3.3% year-on-year — with net profits of US$120 billion and aggregate EBITDA margins improving from 23% to 27% as higher gold, copper, and uranium prices combined with cost discipline to deliver record sector cash generation. Share buybacks surged 252% to US$5.8 billion driven by gold companies at record margins; M&A deal values topped US$70 billion despite a 20% decline in transaction count; and BHP generated US$19.8 billion in operating cash flow while Zijin Mining posted a 128% increase to US$10.5 billion.

headline: LITHIUM PLUNGES TO 10-WEEK LOW: CATL JIANXIAWO RESTART CHATTER HITS 3% OF GLOBAL SUPPLY — CNY 157,000 AND FALLING
snippet: Chinese lithium carbonate prices fell nearly 10% across two trading sessions to CNY 157,000 per tonne — a 10-week low — after Jiangxi province issued a preliminary government land assessment notice for CATL's Jianxiawo mine, which shut in August 2025 when its permit expired and accounts for an estimated 3% of global lithium production. The notice contains no confirmed restart timeline and appears to be a procedural land-use step, but markets priced in near-term resumption: the same mine whose closure helped reignite lithium's multi-year price recovery is now a supply-side headwind precisely when energy storage is structurally shifting the demand mix toward a sixth consecutive annual deficit.

headline: PROSPECTOR METALS TESS ZONE: THREE RIGS, 25,000m AND LAB RESULTS WEEKS AWAY IN YUKON CU-AU TARGET (TSXV:PPP)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Prospector Metals Corp. (TSXV:PPP)
snippet: Prospector Metals Corp. (TSXV:PPP) provided a June 25 update on its 25,000-metre 2026 drill program at the ML Project in Yukon, targeting the TESS Zone that returned 13.79 g/t gold and 1.84% copper over 44 metres in the 2025 discovery. With 15 holes (3,203m) completed — twelve directly testing the TESS NE-SW structural corridor — samples en route to Bureau Veritas in Whitehorse and a third drill rig arriving June 27, initial 2026 assays are expected in coming weeks, making this a near-term catalyst for a high-grade gold-copper discovery that is open along trend and at depth.

headline: KODIAK COPPER CLOSES C$15M OVERSUBSCRIBED CHARITY FLOW-THROUGH — FULLY FUNDED FOR BC PORPHYRY 2026 SEASON (TSXV:KDK)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Kodiak Copper Corp. (TSXV:KDK)
snippet: Kodiak Copper Corp. (TSXV:KDK) closed its upsized private placement June 25 at C$15 million — charity flow-through shares at C$1.271/share with Paradigm Capital as lead agent, oversubscribed from its initial C$10 million target — fully funding the company's 2026 exploration program at its MPD copper-gold porphyry project in British Columbia, one of the province's largest untested porphyry footprints. The oversubscription demonstrates institutional appetite for BC copper-gold development plays even during the current correction, with a potentially structurally significant Section 232 refined copper tariff decision due from Commerce Secretary Lutnick by June 30.

headline: GORILLA GOLD: 31.5 g/t AT SOVEREIGN PLUS NEW LADY MARGARET SHALLOW DISCOVERY — KALGOORLIE HUB ON TWO FRONTS (ASX:GG8)
source_name: Stocks Down Under / Gorilla Gold Mines Ltd (ASX:GG8)
snippet: Gorilla Gold Mines (ASX:GG8) released a dual-front set of drilling results from its North Kalgoorlie Hub in Western Australia: Sovereign growth drilling returned multiple high-grade intervals including 1.2m at 31.5g/t gold from 69.1m in hole STEX192 and 7.6m at 5.1g/t from 251.3m in STEX189, while scout drilling at the new Lady Margaret Prospect — 1km west of Sovereign — hit 2.0m at 5.9g/t gold from just 18.0m in initial hole LMEX010. The Lady Margaret discovery is open in every direction and sits on ground historically known as the Comet Vale district's first 1890s discovery, expanding the lateral exploration footprint of a Hub already hosting 1.2 million ounces at 3.7g/t Au.
